lesson.title: Logical Choices
lesson.driving_question: How can a program check more than one rule at the same time?
lesson.primary_concept_family: and and or combine Boolean conditions into a larger rule.
misconceptions: and needs both conditions to be True.
or needs at least one condition to be True.
Each comparison still needs its own complete expression.
Parentheses can make a combined rule easier to read.

progression.modify_b: let an adult provide an alternative entry reason

code_expectations: Write a complete comparison on each side of and or or.
Use and when both requirements matter.
Use or when either reason is enough.

Repair the comparison variable in the rule. Run the program with a successful and an unsuccessful set of answers.

blocks.definition: A comparison produces True or False. A Boolean condition can be used by if.
and makes one rule from two conditions. Both conditions must be True for the whole rule to be True.
or makes one rule from two conditions. The whole rule is True when at least one condition is True.
Write a complete comparison on each side of and or or. Do not leave a value by itself.
A rule checker tests requirements and displays a clear result. The program can make one decision from several facts.
